A1.justification: Both PDFs describe EgoHOIBench and EgoNCE++. Their complete main texts and Appendices A–D are readable, including equations, tables and figures, allowing reliable comparison across the reorganization.

before.justification: v1 reports original benchmark evaluations, training ablations, feature analyses and qualitative results in the main text and appendices.

after.justification: v3 retains original experimental results and adds classification, model-scaling, cross-LLM benchmark and generation-efficiency results.

M1.justification: The asymmetric objective and visual LoRA adaptation remain. However, v3 Sections 3.3 and C.1 change the stated LaViLa procedure from freezing the entire text encoder to training its word embeddings. Vocabulary substitution becomes an explicit generation alternative, although vocabulary-based generation was already evaluated in v1.

E1.justification: v3 adds EK100-CLS action classification and EgoHOIBench variants with GPT-4o- and DeepSeek-generated candidates, extending task and language-input coverage within the existing egocentric domains. The six principal earlier benchmarks remain, while the EgoMCQ inter/intra diagnostic comparison in v1 Figure 2 disappears.

E2.justification: v3 introduces substantive zero-shot comparisons against HelpingHands and HENASY on EK100-MIR and EGTEA in Table 1, plus HelpingHands and its variant without object supervision in the LaViLa-Large comparison in Table 9. HelpingHands was cited but not evaluated in v1; these comparisons materially expand the competitive baseline coverage.

E3.justification: New protocols include frozen-encoder linear probing, EK100-CLS zero-shot classification conditioned on the ground-truth complementary verb or noun, and LaViLa-Large evaluation. Negative-count experiments extend to 64 negatives and evaluate retrieval metrics. The PND metric is removed. Appendix B.1 also drops the previously stated BLEU-based selection of benchmark candidates, without establishing whether the benchmark was regenerated.

E4.justification: v3 adds cross-LLM benchmark sensitivity, vocabulary-overlap and generation-efficiency analyses, expands loss ablations to retrieval, and extends representation visualizations to text/video embeddings and before/after training. Similarity histograms replace the earlier small similarity-matrix illustration, and the PND analysis is removed. Existing positive/negative-type, data-volume and LoRA-rank ablations are largely retained.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, random seeds, confidence intervals, significance tests or comparable uncertainty estimates. The new histograms describe similarity distributions, not uncertainty in experimental estimates.

E6.justification: v3 adds classification, large-model, efficiency and cross-LLM results; Table 15 reports LaViLa++ action accuracy of 44.63% and 39.15% on GPT-4o and DeepSeek variants, while retaining 63.17% on the original variant. Zero-shot EGTEA mean/top-1 entries change from 31.43/33.02 in v1 Table 10 to 34.0/35.4 in v3 Table 1, alongside revised training. These are revised reported results, not an established same-setting performance gain.

T1.justification: The formally defined PND separation metric in v1 Appendix C.4, Equation 6, is removed. Temperature factors also disappear from displayed Equations 2–4, although the PDFs do not explain whether this is shorthand or a substantive change. No theorem or proof is added.

C1.justification: The central contributions remain the benchmark, asymmetric objective and improved downstream generalization. v3 broadens the advertised method to include vocabulary-generated negatives and extends the stated evaluation scope from six to seven downstream tasks. Its stronger emphasis on temporal understanding uses ActionBench evidence already present in v1.

C2.justification: v3 develops explanations connecting noun clustering to visual similarity and single-frame encoding, and distinguishes preserved object-centered structure from improved video-text matching. Appendix A replaces limitations about stronger LLMs and training from scratch with substantive boundaries concerning non-HOI activities and text-only object supervision. New discussion addresses generator bias, computational tradeoffs and compatibility with object-supervised methods.

D1.justification: v3 adds useful implementation disclosures: explicit #C/#O filtering, spaCy vocabulary extraction, Decord video loading, checkpoint-selection policy and model-specific word-embedding training. It also reports generation hardware and costs in Appendix C.5. These extend an already documented training recipe; the code-access location remains unchanged.

R1.justification: v3 adds literature on object-centered features, single-frame bias, HENASY and newer egocentric pretraining, and explicitly discusses complementarity with HelpingHands. Some earlier temporal-learning and generic LLM references are removed. These refine the existing positioning within egocentric contrastive learning.

P1.justification: The abstract, introduction, benchmark motivation and experimental narrative are extensively rewritten. Related work moves from Section 2 to Section 5, objective diagnosis becomes part of the benchmark section, and substantial results and ablations move into reorganized appendices. Terminology increasingly emphasizes HOI word variations and video-text matching.

P2.justification: v3 substantially redesigns the visual presentation: a new opening illustration, expanded radar charts and embedding plots, similarity histograms, retrieval-scaling plots, and new comparison and analysis tables. The architecture diagram adds trainable word embeddings, the benchmark-construction diagram is removed, and several retained tables and qualitative examples are relocated or reformatted.

improvement.justification: Cross-LLM tests directly examine sensitivity to benchmark construction, while stronger comparators and generation-cost and implementation disclosures improve evidential support and reproducibility. These benefits are tempered by unreconciled LaViLa++ retrieval results: v3 Table 1 reports average mAP/nDCG of 32.0/33.1, while Table 7 retains 31.7/32.3 without clearly distinguishing their settings. The additions support a net improvement, but the reporting ambiguity limits its strength.
